draft.title: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights
card: The United Nations (UN) was formed in 1945, after the Second World War. Its members wanted to prevent such suffering happening again.
In 1948 the UN General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. It set out rights that belong to every person, in every country.
Australia was one of eight countries on the committee that drafted the Declaration. Australia's H. V. Evatt was also President of the General Assembly in 1948, which passed it.
The Declaration is a statement of shared ideals. It is not a treaty, so it does not by itself make a country change its laws.
draft.remember: The 1948 Declaration set out rights for all people. Australia helped draft it, and Evatt led the assembly that passed it.

a.q: What was the main purpose of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, adopted in 1948?
opts: To set out rights for every person after the war's suffering
To make each member country pass new laws straight away
To list the rights of only the countries that won the war
To end the Second World War by setting terms of peace
a.why: The Declaration followed the suffering of the Second World War and set out rights for every person. It was not a treaty with legal duties, and the war had already ended.
a.clue: Think about what the world had just lived through, and who the rights were for.

b.q: Tom says Australia had to change its laws in 1948 because it helped draft the Declaration. What is wrong with his claim?
opts: It was a statement of ideals, not a treaty forcing new laws
Australia was not on the committee that drafted it
It set out rights only for people living in Australia
It was adopted by Australia alone, not by the United Nations
b.why: The Declaration was a shared statement of ideals and did not by itself make any country change its laws. Australia did help draft it and Evatt led the assembly, but that does not turn it into a law.
b.clue: Think about what kind of document the Declaration is.
